page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What causes it
steps.why: Insulin drives sugar out of the blood, so an excess of it empties the blood of the sugar the brain needs.
common_mistakes: Blaming too little insulin. That is diabetes mellitus.
steps.memory_tip: Too much insulin drives the blood sugar too low.
steps.margin_note: Give both causes: the gland and the injection.
lines: Insulin shock is a condition due to
hypersecretion of insulin, or to an
overdose of insulin in a diabetic patient.

steps.label: What it shows
steps.why: The brain has no store of sugar, so a sudden fall in blood glucose affects it first.
common_mistakes: Giving high blood glucose. It is low.
steps.memory_tip: Hypoglycaemia: hypo is low, glycaemia is blood sugar.

lines.text: It shows hypoglycaemia, low blood glucose

insider_note: It is the opposite of diabetes: too much insulin, not too little. Say hypersecretion or over-dosage in the first line.
